how.title: How article improvements work
how.intro: We review how the articles on your website perform in Google Search. When the data shows a clear opportunity to rank better, we rewrite that article, changing only the parts that need it.
steps: Through Google Search Console we track clicks, impressions, click-through rate and rankings for every article.
On each improvement day we rewrite the article with the clearest opportunity. It's prepared the day before, so it's ready for review on the day.
Approve or reject each change one by one. Nothing goes live until you approve, unless auto-approve is on. Flagged rewrites always wait for your review.
Two weeks after an improvement goes live, we compare its clicks and impressions with the two weeks before.
how.eligibility: Articles that already perform well are left alone. To qualify, a page needs at least 90 days in Google Search and real search demand. Pages improved in the last 6 months, or rejected in the last 4 weeks, are skipped. When several pages qualify, the one with the most impressions goes first.

credits.title: Backlink exchange explained
steps: Every site starts with 100 credits, so it can receive backlinks right away.
When one of your articles gives a live backlink, you earn credits equal to your domain rating, up to 25 per backlink.

When you receive a backlink, you spend credits equal to the giving site's domain rating. A link from a stronger site costs more than one of yours earns, so your balance can dip below zero for a while.
While your balance is below zero, incoming backlinks pause. Your new articles keep giving links, which brings it back up automatically.
credits.placement: Links are added inside new articles published by sites in the network, only where the linked page genuinely helps the reader. They are normal (dofollow) links in the text, and they count once we've seen them live on the page.
